entities.name: HIRA Q86HX1
observations: Reviewed UniProt reference identifies Q86HX1 as HIRA from Dictyostelium discoideum; its annotation states periodic repression of histone-gene transcription and replication-independent chromatin assembly (by similarity).
Reference annotation places HIRA in the nucleus and HIR complex; GO annotations include transcription corepressor activity and chromatin remodeling.
The 768-aa supplied sequence matched 100% identity across the query to Q86HX1 in the protein search, while reference protein length is 1,114 aa; supplied sequence may represent a partial sequence.

entities.name: Supplied sequence 768 aa
observations: Sequence-derived mass is approximately 83.6 kDa and theoretical pI 6.93.
Pfam detects a strong N-terminal Beta-prop_CAF1B_HIR1 domain at residues 1–193, four WD40 repeat hits across residues 10–190, and an HIRA_B hit at residues 458–480.

Much of the sequence after the N-terminal domain is compositionally low-complexity and enriched in Ser, Gln, Asn, Gly, and charged residues; this suggests flexible/disordered regions but is not a direct disorder prediction.
